the postoperative migration of the ASA and FFA following total hip arthropathy with a well-fixed PTCS implanted by a line-to-line technique.
the change of stem migration, and the change of functional femoral anteversions of the femur following THA.
the migration of a well-fixed PTCS implanted by line-to-line technique after THA.

a PTCS implanted using the line-to-line implant technique has less axial rotation migration and better functional anteversion after THA than a PTCS implanted with a standard technique.
the line-to-line implant technique of PTCS is associated with less migration and a more favorable functional anteversion of a PTCS.
the PTCS implanted by a line-to-line technique can be expected to be well fixed and stable in the early stage after THA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a PTCS implanted with the line-to-line implant technique can be used in the treatment of patients with preoperative external rotation femoral contracture.

the anatomical and the functional anteversion angle of the femur were significantly changed by THA, and the change in axial stem rotation was significantly associated with the preoperative external rotational deformity of the femur.
the PTCS implanted by line-to-line technique is an effective method for restoring the anatomical and the functional anteversion of a femur.
